o1.said: A robot explores a warehouse it has never seen. It is a Ross two demo for students, and three p p is its world, its sensors and its screen.

w1.said: The simulator is one C plus plus node. three p p draws the warehouse, and plays the robot's hardware.

w2.said: The lidar is a ray caster against the scene. The camera is a second render, from the robot's own eye.

g1.said: Everything else only sees Ross two topics. So each node can be written in the language that suits it.

g2.said: A mapper turns laser scans into a map. An explorer picks a frontier, the edge of what is known, and plans a path there.

g3.said: A safety monitor, in C plus plus, sits between the planner and the motors. It stops the robot before it hits anything.

g4.said: A cone spotter finds traffic cones in the camera image, and uses the lidar to place them on the map.

g5.said: And the dashboard is three p p again, this time from Python. It draws what the robot believes.

b1.said: Left, the world as it is. Right, the world as the robot believes it to be, built from its own scans.

b2.said: It drives to a frontier, the map grows, and it picks the next one. When none are left, it drives home.

f1.said: In C plus plus, C make fetches three p p and links it like any other library. The render loop keeps the main thread, and Ross two spins on a second one.

f2.said: In Python, it is a wheel from pie P I, installed next to Ross two by the same tool.

u1.said: Running it takes three commands. Pixie brings Ross two from Robo Stack, and three p p with it.

a1.said: The demo was built in two to three hours by an A I coding agent, Claude Code, with a person steering.

a2.said: Sub-agents wrote the Python packages in parallel, against one written interface. The result was checked in headless renders, full runs and unit tests.

a3.said: The first version worked, and looked like a game from the nineties. One line of feedback later, it looked like this.

e1.said: Ross two carries the messages. three p p is the world, the sensors and the screen.
